## Natural history notes

A small chocolate-brown moth characterized by four thin pale lines running across the forewings, giving it a subtly striped appearance. In Florida, it is found in the eastern coastal plain in wooded wetlands, shrublands, forest edges, and other humid habitats where plants such as maleberry and swamp dog-hobble may occur. Adults are day-flying and may be seen resting on vegetation or visiting flowers, while the caterpillars are associated with ericaceous shrubs and help move plant material into the broader insect food web.
